chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Miles Davis: the parking-lot anecdote
summary: Asked for funny stories, Gil recalls waiting for the car with Miles when a stranger handed Miles a parking ticket.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I got this idea from my friend Owen Dodson (Louts?) and the poet, playwright who is writing a fascinating book which he calls "The Gossip Book". And it's filled with absolutely marvellous stories, quoted anecdotes, about the people from the world of art. And I'm wondering if you were to write such a book what some of your favorite anecdotes might be that you would include. Can you think of some stories that you just love? About very funny things that happened along the way? There must have been some. Miles Davis probably has provided you with some.
Miles was always funny. I can't ever think of anything that he would say except that he was funny.
It's not just a matter of what he might just say as such, but I think that there are ( ?).

Well most of the, a lot of the things that are funny like the old saying, who pays for your jokes? Somebody's always the butt of a joke. And those that are funny actually are funny because you are picking on somebody or you want to laugh instead of cry.

So I mean I really can't as far as, but when I first met Miles, Davis, we were waiting in a parking lot one night for his car. He had a European car at that time too. Maybe slightly smaller than the last one that he just smashed up, but it was a big car for, a Ferrari or something you know, a $20,000 car.
We were standing in the parking lot waiting for the car when this character comes up. It was in the evening I guess, he'd been out to the Latin Quarter or something and a big red faced guy from
Texas or probably somewhere like that and Miles and I were standing waiting for our car and he hands Miles the ticket to his car and of course, you know, go get my car. (LAUGHTER).
I wont ask you what Miles said. (LAUGHTER).
Nothing, just straight ahead like that. Just straight ahead like that never even, like pretend the man wasn't even talking to him. (LAUGHTER).
The man would keep trying to say it you know and (just about then the man came with our car?). (LAUGHTER).

And so he was standing there when Miles got into his Ferrari. (LAUGHTER). That's as bad as when I got on the elevator one day here at this hotel and I had my keys in my hand. And the woman looked me and she said, oh, are you the new housekeeper? To go through this kind of thing all the time.
People are conditioned like that, raised like that.
You don't have to like it but but you can understand it but you don't have to like it.
